 A little-known IRS process can reduce your upfront investment in clean energy projects, according to Eric Woodroof, Ph.D., CEM. Nov. 6, 2026 Add Us On Google 
 ID 46637182 © Kemaltaner | Dreamstime.com 6aeccd24ba43d5cc9906c5fc Dreamstime Xxl 46637182 Some energy projects still qualify for tax credits, including energy storage technology. A new report by Eric Woodroof, Ph.D., CEM, suggests that putting certain energy projects into service can allow you to take advantage of a formal IRS process in which some of your previously paid taxes are refunded if you invest in certain energy projects, thus reducing your upfront investment and delivering the benefits of accelerated depreciation. Download the report to learn how the process works.
 Note: Dr. Woodroof is not delivering tax advice. Consult a tax attorney/CPA for tax advice.
